🎥🚕: Taxi Driver (1976)

Travis Bickle is a lonely Vietnam War veteran working long nights as a taxi driver through the streets of New York City. Disconnected from the people around him and increasingly disturbed by the crime and corruption he witnesses, Travis becomes obsessed with the idea that the city needs to be cleaned up.

His isolation deepens after an unsuccessful attempt to connect with Betsy, a woman working on a political campaign. As his frustration grows, Travis becomes increasingly fixated on taking drastic action, while also becoming determined to help Iris, a vulnerable teenage girl trapped in a dangerous situation.

Dark, psychological, and unsettling, Taxi Driver explores loneliness, alienation, obsession, and a man’s deteriorating relationship with the world around him as he searches for purpose in a city he no longer understands.

source_details.synopsis: Taxi Driver is a 1976 American neo-noir psychological drama film directed by Martin Scorsese and written by Paul Schrader. Set in New York City in a time of urban decay following the Vietnam War, it stars Robert De Niro as taxi driver Travis Bickle, whose mental state deteriorates as he works nights in the city, eventually having a mental breakdown and becoming a vigilante. The film also features Jodie Foster, Cybill Shepherd, Harvey Keitel, Peter Boyle, Leonard Harris and Albert Brooks (in his first feature film role).
